source: NCERT-aligned UPSC Ecology & Environment (Class XI), Ch. 6 (Environmental Pollution).

sections.heading: 1. Air Pollution
points: **Air pollution** = harmful substances in the air (particulate matter **PM2.5/PM10**, SO₂, NOx, CO, ozone, lead).
Sources: vehicles, industries, burning of fossil fuels/crop residue.
Effects: respiratory diseases, **smog**, acid rain, reduced visibility; **National Air Quality Index (AQI)** monitors it.
**Bhopal Gas Tragedy (1984)** — methyl isocyanate (MIC) leak — worst industrial disaster.

sections.heading: 2. Water Pollution
points: Contamination by sewage, industrial effluents, fertilisers/pesticides, plastics.
**Eutrophication** — nutrient enrichment (N, P) → algal blooms → oxygen depletion → death of aquatic life.
**Biological Oxygen Demand (BOD)** — high BOD indicates high organic pollution.
**Biomagnification** — toxins (DDT, mercury) concentrate up the food chain (e.g. **Minamata disease** — mercury).

sections.heading: 3. Soil, Noise and Other Pollution
points: **Soil pollution** — chemicals, plastics, industrial/e-waste; reduces fertility.
**Noise pollution** — measured in **decibels (dB)**; causes stress, hearing loss.
**Radioactive, thermal, and plastic pollution** (microplastics); **e-waste** is a growing problem.
**Solid waste management** — 3 Rs: **Reduce, Reuse, Recycle**; segregation and composting.

sections.heading: 4. Control Measures
points: Air: catalytic converters, cleaner fuels (CNG, BS-VI norms), scrubbers/ESP (electrostatic precipitators), afforestation.
Water: effluent treatment plants, sewage treatment, banning harmful discharge; **Namami Gange**.
Legislation: **Water Act (1974), Air Act (1981), Environment Protection Act (1986)**; the **Central/State Pollution Control Boards (CPCB/SPCB)**.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Air pollutants: PM2.5/PM10, SO₂, NOx, CO; AQI monitors air quality.
Eutrophication = nutrient enrichment → algal bloom → oxygen depletion.
High BOD = high organic water pollution; biomagnification (DDT, mercury).
Minamata disease = mercury poisoning; Bhopal Gas Tragedy (1984) = MIC leak.
Noise in decibels; 3 Rs = Reduce, Reuse, Recycle.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Eutrophication depletes oxygen** in water (algal blooms), killing aquatic life.
**High BOD indicates high pollution** (more oxygen demand).
**Biomagnification** = toxins increase **up** the food chain (top predators most affected).
**Minamata disease = mercury**; **Bhopal Tragedy (1984) = methyl isocyanate (MIC)**.
